core_memory.travel_experiences: I've always been fascinated by exploring new places. As a fourth-year Computer Science major, I have to be strategic about planning my trips. I've managed to squeeze in some adventures that have given me some of my favorite memories so far.
core_memory.sailing_trip: Sailing trip off the coast of Maine with a friend before my sophomore year. Explored coastal towns, sailed past islands with pine trees, learned about navigation using GPS devices and star charts. Enjoyed fresh lobster rolls at a small dockside shack.
core_memory.japan_trip: Japan trip during my junior year's winter break. Explored Tokyo's Akihabara and electronics stores, marveled at Shibuya intersection, and enjoyed incredible food. Then headed to Kyoto, where I visited shrines and temples and spotted geishas in Gion. Felt like stepping back into an older era.
core_memory.europe_trip: Family vacation to Europe last summer. Explored London's history and enjoyed a musical in the West End. Then, we took a train to Paris, where I strolled along the Seine River near Notre-Dame with a croissant. The pastries were amazing! We spent a day at the Louvre, which was incredible.

archival_memory.research_experience: I've been involved in undergrad research since my sophomore year, which has been an eye-opening experience. It's given me insight into how knowledge is created in the tech world. I initially didn't see myself going down the research route, but a professor noticed my skills in bridging technical coding with user experience and suggested I apply for a research assistant position in a data visualization lab. I was hesitant at first, but it turned out to be a great decision.
